A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeRAF and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–O. The corresponding material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original acoustic and visual synthesis experiments on SoundSpaces, RAF, and RWAVS, including ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The NeRF backbone, voxel-grid conditioning, acoustic network, joint training objectives, and Griffin-Lim reconstruction are unchanged. The dataset-specific adaptations in Appendices A and J were already present in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SoundSpaces scenes, RAF rooms, and RWAVS environments. Sparse-observation, unseen-source, furniture-proximity, and multi-scene scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same respective comparator sets for SoundSpaces and RAF, including the listed codec and neural-method variants. RWAVS Table A2 retains INRAS, NAF, ViGAS, and AV-NeRF; visual comparisons still use Nerfacto.

E3.justification: Data splits, view counts, STFT settings, metrics, training budgets, and the unseen-source evaluation remain unchanged. RAF wording changes from 'resampled' to 'sampled' at 48 kHz, consistent with Appendix C already specifying that this rate is retained; this does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The grid and loss ablations, few-shot tests, furniture analysis, unseen-source test, and joint-versus-separate and multi-scene training comparisons occur in both versions. Rewriting Appendices N–O adds no new analysis or experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state that each experiment is conducted six times and results are averaged. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a revised uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and A1–A6 retain their numerical entries, and the figures retain the same results and examples. For instance, NeRAF's SoundSpaces T60/C50/EDT remain 2.14/0.38/0.010 in Table 1, and Appendix M retains the unseen-source results.

T1.justification: The field definitions, rendering formulation, loss equations, energy-decay derivation, and metric formulas in Equations (1)–(17) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about 3D-conditioned acoustic synthesis, cross-modal visual improvements, data efficiency, and independent modality rendering. The revised experimental overview merely mentions the multi-scene experiment already reported in v3.

C2.justification: The interpretations of grid conditioning, loss tradeoffs, RWAVS performance, and joint training remain the same, as do the static-scene and per-scene NeRF limitations. Appendices N–O explain existing comparisons more explicitly without introducing a new interpretation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Section 4 redirects readers from supplementary material to the project page for demonstration videos, changing resource-access guidance. Architecture, implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning against earlier acoustic fields and audio-visual methods. Related-work edits concern wording and capitalization.

P1.justification: v4 revises affiliations, contact information, and acknowledgments; standardizes headings and cross-references; rewrites the experimental overview; and expands the prose in Appendices N–O. The overall section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds conference headers, adjusts spacing and captions, and downscales several embedded figures while preserving their content. No figures or tables are added or removed. A small stray numeral appears beside Table 1.

improvement.justification: The clearer experimental overview, expanded explanations in Appendices N–O, and revised video pointer provide small editorial benefits. They largely restate existing information, while methods, evidence, conclusions, and limitations remain unchanged. These benefits and minor presentation blemishes do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
